node.title: Find the shortest word in the English Language with: a b c d e f
node.author: usemodperl
node.doctext:
Edit: Not going to edit this node because of replies but Eily noticed there is an extra single quote at the end of my port :-/

[https://www.reddit.com/r/programming/comments/8vi24p/getting_back_into_development_at_50_after_15/e1ojtor/?context=3|This recent post in r/programming] poses an interesting question for a bit of golf: "What is the shortest word in the English Language which contains: a b c d e f?" Some Junk™ code was posted to figure this out and my Perl version is a bit shorter. I know you perl better than me, if you do, and can see how else to do this:

The Junk Code: sorted([w.strip() for w in open('/usr/share/dict/words', 'r').readlines() if set(list('abcdef')).issubset(set(list(w.strip())))], key=lambda x: len(x)) My Perl Port: open$:,"){next unless/(?=.*a)(?=.*b)(?=.*c)(?=.*d)(?=.*e)(?=.*f)/i;push@_,$_}@_=sort{length$a<=>length$b}@_'

For your convenience:

Print the list: open$:,"){next unless/(?=.*a)(?=.*b)(?=.*c)(?=.*d)(?=.*e)(?=.*f)/i;push@_,$_}print for sort{length$a<=>length$b}@_ Print the word: open$:,"){next unless/(?=.*a)(?=.*b)(?=.*c)(?=.*d)(?=.*e)(?=.*f)/i;push@_,$_}for(sort{length$a<=>length$b}@_){print;last} Compare length of Perl to Junk: #!/usr/bin/perl -lw use strict; my $PERL = <<'PERL'; open$:,"){next unless/(?=.*a)(?=.*b)(?=.*c)(?= .*d)(?=.*e)(?=.*f)/i;push@_,$_}@_=sort{length$a<=>length$b}@_' PERL { no strict; $JUNK = < Of course different versions of dict give different results...
